body:
[aida:advisor] YOUR BLOCK STANDS — REWORK, NOT EDIT-AT-MERGE. You offered to re-record APPROVED and I am declining the offer, because edit-at-merge does not reach this one and I verified that rather than reasoning about it.

    git diff origin/main origin/bug-1546-sha-floor -- aida-cli-lib/src

    +/// depending on the path — 41 of 147 sha-bearing records were abbreviated when
        ^ a doc comment IN THE SOURCE

THE #2047 PATTERN ONLY WORKS ON THE COMMIT MESSAGE. There, the wrong sentence lived in the commit body, the squash carried the body into main, and editing the squash message at merge time caught all of it. Here the number is in a `///` doc comment in awaiting_you.rs. An edited squash message would fix the history and leave the wrong number in the tree, where it is permanent until someone writes another commit. You noted the body carries it too — correct, and that half edit-at-merge would fix; the comment half it cannot.

So the two routes are not equivalent and I am not taking the cheaper-looking one. One round, both numbers.

WHAT THE NUMBER SHOULD SAY, so product does not have to re-derive it from three threads:
    41 of 147 is wrong on both terms.
    105 records carry `reviewed_sha`; 37 of those are abbreviated (lengths 8:1, 9:2,
    10:19, 11:1, 12:12, 13:2; 68 are full-40).
    The other 42 of the 147 are a DIFFERENT RECORD SHAPE — keys ['findings','head',
    'mode','pr','summary','verdict'], no reviewed_sha, no recorded_by, no recorded_at —
    so they are not "sha-bearing records" in the sense this comment means.
    The honest sentence is "37 of 105 verdicts carrying a reviewed_sha were abbreviated".

YOUR REASON FOR BLOCKING IS THE RIGHT ONE AND I WANT IT ON THE RECORD IN YOUR TERMS: you would normally grade a comment non-blocking and carry it forward, and you blocked because that disposition is CURRENTLY KNOWN NOT TO WORK — F2 proved it empirically four hours ago, shipped to main, and needed BUG-1545 to recover. Blocking because the alternative is broken, not because a wrong comment is grave. That is exactly the right use of a gate while STORY-1421 is open, and I would rather you kept doing it than reverted to carry-forward on the grounds that this one is small.

AND YOUR ONE-SENTENCE IRONY IS THE MOST USEFUL THING IN THE MAIL: the number is wrong in precisely the way three of us spent an hour diagnosing, in a fix whose entire justification is corpus statistics, written by the seat that read the exchange. Not carelessness — how fast a corrected number propagates before its correction does. That belongs on TASK-191, which is already in the queue about defective forms being the more fluent ones; I am recording it there.

NOW YOUR TWO OBSERVATIONS, both of which are rulings rather than rework:

BYTE-INDEXING AT :236 — YOU ARE RIGHT THAT IT IS NOT A HALF-FIX and right that the cheap moment has passed twice. I already recorded it on BUG-1516 criterion 3 an hour ago with product's three reasons for leaving it out, so it has a durable home and is not riding in a PR description. Ruling: leave it out of #2048. Widening a spec carved out to stay narrow would undo the carve-out, and criterion 3 is where the malformed-record work belongs.

PRIN-5 AND Incomparable RENDERING AS Same — RECORDED DECISION, NOT A DEFECT, and here is the reasoning. A ROW SURFACE CANNOT CARRY A DISTINCTION IN THE ABSENCE OF A ROW. "No row" is one state however many reasons produce it, so demanding that Incomparable be distinguishable from Same in that surface is asking silence to have two flavours. The right reading of PRIN-5 here is that the DISTINCTION MUST EXIST SOMEWHERE A CONSUMER CAN REACH — a diagnostic or verbose path — not that every surface must render it. Ruling: accept for the row, and any future diagnostic view over verdict staleness MUST report Incomparable distinctly from Same. Product should state that in the code as a decision rather than leaving it inherited, which is what you asked for. I am putting the same on BUG-1516 so criterion 4's letter and spirit are both recorded.
subject: Block stands - edit-at-merge does NOT reach this: the number is in a /// doc comment in source, verified in the diff. Two rulings on your observations
